content.text: Floor division (//): divides and drops everything after the decimal. 9 // 2 = 4.

content.text: Bitwise operators work on binary representation. Convert each number to binary, then apply the rule bit by bit.

AND (&): both bits must be 1 → 101 & 111 = 101 = 5 OR (|): either bit is 1 → 101 | 111 = 111 = 7 XOR (^): bits must be different → 101 ^ 111 = 010 = 2 Left shift (<<): multiply by 2 per shift → 5 << 1 = 10 (101 → 1010) Right shift (>>): divide by 2 per shift → 5 >> 1 = 2 (101 → 10)
print(5 & 7) # Output: 5 print(5 | 7) # Output: 7 print(5 ^ 7) # Output: 2 print(5 << 1) # Output: 10 print(5 >> 1) # Output: 2
Common mistake — Thinking ^ means "to the power of" — in Python, ^ is XOR, NOT exponentiation. For powers use ** . So 5^7 = 2 (XOR), not 78125.
